We have isolated a cDNA from a mouse brain library which contains a complete open reading frame for a mouse homologue of human neurofibromatose type 2 gene.
The mouse homologue of human neurofibromatostis type 2 gene (NF2) was isolated and sequenced.
the mouse homologue (Schn) of the neurofibroma- tosis type 2 (Nf2) tumor suppressor gene is highly consenved.

the molecular basis of the human neurofibromatous diseases.
the molecular genetics of neurofibromatose type 2 (Nf2), a genetic disease which predisposes individuals to the development of schwanno- mas, meningiomas and ependymomas.

the molecular analysis of the NF2 tumor suppressor gene and its protein product, the schwannomin, in order to better understand the function of the NF2 protein and the mechanism by which it acts as a tumor suppressor.

the mouse homologue to the human NF2 gene is a highly conserved protein with a predicted secondary structure similar to that of other members of the band-4.1 supergene family.
the NF2 mouse gene is the first member of a novel class of tumor suppressor gene that encodes for a protein which is involved in the regulation of membrane cytoskeleton interactions.
the NF2 protein is highly conserved among species, suggesting a critical role in the development of the nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NF2 tumor suppressor gene is highly consered and is expressed in a variety of mouse tissues.

we have isolated a full length cDNA of the mouse homolog of the NF2 tumor suppressor gene, that we have determined its structure, its expression pattern and its homology with other band 4. 1 family members and that we have determined the predicted amino acid sequence of the SCH.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the NF2 tumor suppressor gene is highly consed in mice and that the protein product of the gene, schwannomin, appears to act as an adaptor molecule linking the plasma membrane with the cytoskeletal network of the cell.
the NF2 protein, which we have called schwannomin, is highly conserved between humans and mice, and is a member of the large family of band 4. 1 proteins.
